title: Ancient Egyptian Horus tablet from Tanis San el Hagar dated 332 BC – AD 395
text: A limestone tablet with an incised standing figure of Horus, facing right as a hawk headed human figure wearing the Double Crown and holding a sceptre. Behind his head and body is a smaller seated figure, probably Nefertum, who holds a sceptre. Horus stands on something, possibly crocodiles, but there is wear to the stone. No traces of any inscription and back of stone roughly shaped.

title: Ancient Egyptian Taweret amulet from Amarna dated 1550 – 1295 BC
text: Pale blue green Taweret amulet, represented by a hippopotamus with the back of a Nile crocodile and human breats. Suspension loop at top, now broken. Standing figure, facing right, flat back.

title: Ancient Egyptian seal amulet from Matmar dated 2181 – 2160 BC
text: A blue glazed faience seal amulet with a hole through it. back in the shape of a hawk head, Horus. Oval shaped base incised with the design of two quadrupeds, one inverted, which could be crocodiles.
Published references: Brunton  Matmar  p 49  pl XXVI  reg  pl XXXIII  30

title: Ancient Egyptian Horus figurine from Saqqara dated 700 – 200 BC
text: A faience Cippus figurine, now blue and red, of Horus the Child. The head has moulded features, and there is a scarab on the top of the head. Hawks flank his head, standing on plaques on his shoulders, and two protective deities, Isis and Nephthys, are visible down his sides. His arms are bent across his chest, and appear to hold two snakes. On the back of the piece is incised the figure of a winged female protective deity, with a sun’s disc and horns on her head. She stands on what may be crocodiles, which are wrapped around the figure to appear at the front under the feet of the male figure. There is a hole for suspension running through the back of the figure’s head.

title: Ancient Egyptian Sobek amulet from Saqqara dated 664 – 332 BC
text: A green faience Sobek, a crocodile amulet. Flat base, hole for suspension through the mouth, ridges on its back.
Published references: Martin  The Sacred Animal Necropolis  p 23  cat no 127

title: Ancient Egyptian animal figurine
text: One of four black stone animal figurine fragments. Possibly a crocodile amulet although there is no detail. There is a hole through one end for suspension. On the flat side there is decoration including the head of a figure.

title: Ancient Egyptian amulet
text: Steatite amulet depicting Horus and the crocodiles. Worn to protect the owner from crocodiles and against the evil eye. Carved and incised with image of Horus standing on a crocodile’s back. The reverse is inscribed with heiroglyphs.

title: Ancient Egyptian sticks from Kom Ombo Aswan dated 332 – 30 BC
text: Four pieces wooden sticks covered in resin. From the three unwrapped mummified newly hatched crocodiles from a tomb near Kom Ombo. Two long sticks with two smaller fragments.

title: Supporting material lantern slide dated AD 1900s
text: Lantern slide with an etching of an idyllic Nile scene: round passepartout, crocodiles in papyrus swamp in foreground, palm trees, boat on Nile and pyramids in background. large emblem EGYPT on architrave “suspended” from top of image with fan as sundisc below. Printed label on top of spine “1 Introductory” Printed label in corner “Egypt” Manufacturer’s label

title: Ancient Egyptian mummy board of Nefsekhet from Faiyum Gurob or Illahun dated 380 – 250 BC
text: Wooden coffin or mummy board with painted face, wig and clothing with funerary inscription of a woman, Nefsekhet, the daughter of Satsobek.
